definition: A softcore or artistically framed film intended to arouse sexual desire, typically less explicit than hardcore pornography.
notes: Used as a category label in video-on-demand platforms and former video rental stores to distinguish softcore from hardcore 'pornofilm'; the framing implies aesthetic or narrative packaging around the sexual content.

definition: Eroticism; the quality or atmosphere of sexual arousal; also used as a media-catalog section label for softcore content.
notes: Functions both as an abstract noun ('de erotiek van de situatie') and as a content-genre label; lower perceived crudeness than 'porno' because the framing implies aesthetic distance rather than raw explicitness.

definition: A retail shop selling sex toys, pornographic materials, lingerie, and other adult products.
notes: Carries minimal stigma in the Netherlands; Amsterdam's openly operating seksshops are a global tourist landmark; the word appears matter-of-factly in mainstream Dutch journalism and city-center signage.

definition: Any object designed for sexual stimulation or pleasure; a sex toy; the diminutive suffix '-tje' softens the register.
notes: Mapped to vibrator as the closest registry concept; the Dutch term is category-generic for all sex toys; the '-tje' diminutive normalizes it enough that it appears in mainstream Dutch retail advertising (e.g. Bol.com, Kruidvat) without scandal.

definition: A penis-shaped insertable sex toy not designed to be worn; direct loanword from English.
notes: Identical spelling to English; appears in Van Dale (the authoritative Dutch dictionary) and in sex-education materials; the Dutch have no native coinage, reflecting early adoption of the English term.

definition: A vibrating device for sexual stimulation; shares spelling with the generic technical sense of any vibrating machine.
notes: Technical-sounding spelling suppresses perceived crudeness; sold openly in Dutch drugstore chains (Kruidvat, Etos) and general retailers; advertised without restriction in mainstream Dutch media.

definition: A magazine containing sexually explicit photographs or content; a pornographic magazine.
notes: Recognition declining with the collapse of print pornography; physical seksmagazines were sold openly at Dutch kiosks, railway station newsstands, and petrol stations through the 1990s; digital distribution has largely displaced the format.

definition: A website dedicated to pornographic content; a porn site.
notes: Standard Dutch compound (no hyphen or space); used matter-of-factly in Dutch journalism, parliamentary debate, and media-literacy curricula when discussing online pornography consumption.

definition: Sexual activity conducted over webcam, either as a paid performance for an audience or privately between consenting partners.
notes: The single compound form 'webcamseks' is the dominant Dutch spelling; context determines whether commercial or private use is meant; appears in Dutch news reporting on online sex work and digital safety.

definition: A woman who performs sexual or erotic acts live on webcam for a paying audience; direct loanword from English.
notes: Used without modification from English; no native Dutch coinage has displaced it; appears in Dutch reporting on online sex work, digital exploitation, and creator-economy discussions.

definition: A man who performs sexual or erotic acts live on webcam for a paying audience; the male equivalent of camgirl.
notes: Significantly less frequent than 'camgirl' in Dutch usage, mirroring the industry's gender asymmetry; no native Dutch coinage; lower recognition reflects lower market share of male performers relative to female.

definition: The OnlyFans subscription platform; in Dutch usage also a common noun shorthand for online explicit content creation or sex work.
notes: Used as both a proper noun and a common noun ('ze heeft een onlyfans'); fully normalized in Dutch tabloid celebrity coverage and broadcast media by 2022; lowercased common-noun use signals genericization.

definition: A male pornographic film performer; a male porn actor.
notes: Compound of 'porno' and the masculine-gendered 'acteur' (from French); relatively low shock value in Dutch media contexts where pornography is discussed pragmatically rather than morally.

definition: A female pornographic film performer; a female porn actress.
notes: Feminine form using the French/Italian '-trice' suffix via 'actrice'; the standard Dutch term for a female porn performer; used without particular euphemism in journalism and online discourse.

definition: A pornographic performer of any gender with recognized fame or notoriety within the industry; a porn star.
notes: Gender-neutral by default; implies a higher industry profile than 'pornoacteur/actrice'; used freely in mainstream Dutch tabloids and celebrity gossip contexts; the 'ster' (star) suffix connotes fame rather than mere participation.

definition: The standard Dutch word for a condom; a latex sheath worn on the penis during sex to prevent pregnancy and STI transmission.
notes: The official and universally used term; taught in schools from age 10–12, prominently featured in Dutch public health campaigns (e.g. Soa Aids Nederland); virtually no stigma attached to saying the word in any register.

definition: Informal Dutch word for a condom; literally 'little hood' or 'little cap'.
notes: Likely derived from French 'capote' (hooded cloak, also a condom term in French) → Dutch 'kapot' + diminutive '-je'; the '-tje' gives it a friendly, non-clinical feel; widely used across all age groups in casual speech; no negative connotation.

definition: Dated Dutch slang for a condom; literally 'little rubber', analogous to British English 'rubber'.
notes: Derived from 'gummi' (rubber/latex); common from the post-WWII era through the early 1980s; largely displaced by 'condoom' and 'kapotje' among speakers under 50; still recognized by older generations; the dated register makes it mildly humorous when used by younger speakers.

definition: Colloquial term for the oral contraceptive pill; used with the definite article as 'de pil'.
notes: Almost invariably used with the definite article 'de pil'; the Netherlands was among the first countries in the world to widely adopt oral contraception following the 1960s introduction; 'de pil' carries no shame and is referenced freely in any social context.

definition: Contraception; the standard Dutch medical and public-health term for pregnancy-prevention methods.
notes: Used freely in school curricula, government health campaigns, and broadcast media; the Netherlands has among Europe's highest rates of contraceptive use, and the word appears with the same neutrality as 'vaccination' or 'hygiene'.

definition: A contraceptive device or method; literally 'precautionary means' or 'preventive means'.
notes: Formal compound (voor + behoedsmiddel, 'fore-safeguard-means'); more legalistic/clinical register than 'anticonceptie'; recognition declining as 'anticonceptie' and specific product names dominate modern usage; still found in formal health documentation.

definition: Informal Dutch term for an intrauterine device; literally 'little spiral', referencing the coiled appearance of earlier IUD designs.
notes: Directly analogous to British English 'coil'; the diminutive '-tje' makes the device sound harmless and approachable; used by patients, GPs, and gynecologists alike; 'IUD' is the clinical co-term but 'spiraaltje' dominates everyday speech across all registers.

definition: International medical acronym for intrauterine device; used in Dutch clinical, pharmaceutical, and policy contexts.
notes: The English-origin acronym is used unchanged in Dutch medical literature and prescriptions; 'spiraaltje' is vastly preferred in everyday patient communication; 'IUD' appears primarily in clinical guidelines, package inserts, and health journalism.

definition: The withdrawal method of contraception; the Latin term used in Dutch clinical, educational, and journalistic contexts.
notes: Identical to the English/Latin phrase; the diaeresis in 'coïtus' marks a vowel hiatus per Dutch orthographic convention; colloquially glossed as 'eruit trekken' (pulling out) in everyday Dutch speech; taught in sex-ed as a method with high failure rate.

definition: Emergency contraceptive pill taken after unprotected sex to prevent pregnancy; a direct calque of English 'morning-after pill'.
notes: Semi-anglicized compound dominant in everyday Dutch speech; clinical alternative is 'noodanticonceptiepil' or 'noodanticonceptie'; available without prescription at Dutch pharmacies (apotheek); the English-derived form reflects the term's arrival in Dutch via Anglo-American public health discourse.
